#4018. Metro 2039 goes back to its Metro underground roots, with a story shaped by the war in Ukraine and the people who suffer it

Metro 2039 takes us back to the tunnels of the Moscow Metro where, fittingly, Nazi ideology never died.

The Metro series is finally, officially back with a new installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

What won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

The game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

The new protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

Today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.

#4017. The siren call of user-generated content has caught Dead by Daylight in its snare, as Behaviour Interactive outline a big revamp update slated for next year

Weather, new models, better maps, it'll have it all

The promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.

"What if you could create your own Dead by Daylight experiences?" explains a blog post recapping the plans for how the game is going to change. "As one of the most exciting updates coming in 2027, the Dead by Daylight Workshop will open the doors to user-created content in some incredible ways. From designing your own Maps and importing custom assets, to modifying game rules, objectives, and even creating entirely new modes, the possibilities are vast."

The post goes on to note that anything created in the workshop will "exist separately from all our classic modes, with dedicated creation tools and moderation provided to ensure experienced modders have everything they need to do their best work, and all submissions meet our official guidelines." I am always hesitant when it comes to UGC faff, because the ability to make your own custom Debbie Daylight maps might sound promising, but people do actually have to engage with them for the whole thing to work. It's just putting a hat on a hat!

Anyway, the workshop isn't the only thing Behaviour have in the works. For one, the game is getting a big visual overhaul. You can expect lighting improvements, more detailed assets and "tons of atmospheric touches," alongside revamps of particular maps like the Temple of Purgation and Backwater Swamp. Killers and survivors will be getting some TLC too by "improving character textures, proportions, hair, and animations to make them look and feel more lifelike. That includes updated character rigs, new motion capture, and new facial animation technology designed to better express a character’s fear, pain, and struggles over the course of a Trial."

Beyond all of that, a dynamic weather system is coming to the game, meaning you'll now have to deal with the likes of rain, thunderstorms, snow and heavy wind, all of which can impact matches. Onboarding for newer folks should be getting some improvements too, with the addition of a "more cinematic introduction, clearer explanations and tutorials of game mechanics, and a more gradual introduction," to the game. All of this will be coming in one big update sometime in 2027, so, keep your eyes peeled for whenever that drops.

We're well under two weeks from the launch of Diablo 4's next expansion, Lord of Hatred, but there's more yet to be said.

Diablo 4 is mere days away from the launch of its biggest expansion yet, and Blizzard wants to make sure it got one last chance to tell you about it. Lord of Hatred is the follow-up to 2024’s Vessel of Hatred, and it’s set to arrive on April 28.

Next week, however, we’re getting an updated look at the new content as part of a livestream. This is the Developer Update kind; the meaty, information-dense show anyone who follows Diablo’s livestreams should be familiar with.

The next Developer Update is set for Thursday, April 23. It’ll kick off at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 6pm GMT. The show will, naturally, focus on Lord of Hatred. In particular, we’re getting another look at the expansion content that hasn’t been given the same level of coverage as the bigger features.

Everyone knows about the new Skovos region, the Warlock class (and the Paladin before that), but we haven’t seen much from the other gameplay-altering features that affect a lot of the core flow.

In next week’s showcase, Blizzard will show off the updated and expanded skill trees - which come to all classes, the Talisman system, and the gear-altering Horadric Cube. War Plans, the new make-your-own-endgame feature will be discussed, too.

More interestingly, we’re also going to hear about the new season kicking off right alongside the launch of Lord of Hatred. A short, in-betweener season is currently live in Diablo 4, and it’s going to end right as the next one/the expansion launch.

And, of course, the show won’t end before the team takes a few questions from chat, as is tradition. If you want to catch it live, you’ll be able to do so on Diablo’s official YouTube, Twitch, Twitter, and TikTok channels.

#4015. PS Plus Essential's Next Update Looks a Bit Better in Japan Than the Rest of the World

It’s all subjective, of course, but Japan’s PS Plus Essential update for December 2026 looks a little bit better than what we’re getting in the west.

Now if we’re looking at pure value here, the Japanese lineup is objectively better: the Bleach game retails for $59.99, while Amnesia is $24.99. The former is also available on PS5 and PS4, whereas the latter is only available for PS4 (although you can of course play it on PS5 via backwards compatibility).

Bleach is also newer, having released in 2025, while Amnesia is from 2023.

But it does ultimately all come down to taste, I suppose; survival horror fans may be much happier with Frictional’s title – especially if they have no real interest in anime. I suppose the lineup in Japan does lack variety, as you’re getting two very similar titles from Bandai Namco there.

Amnesia: The Bunker did release in Japan, so I’m not entirely sure why the lineup is different between regions.

Sony is putting a lot of marketing into its domestic region at the moment, as it tries to reverse its flagging fortunes. It’s also just launched a new PS Portal there, and is putting a pretty big promotional campaign behind it. Maybe it thinks this lineup will be more enticing to Japanese players.

Interesting stuff, though, which selection would you have preferred? I’ve had the Bleach game on my wishlist for a little while, so I think I would have rather got that – but I can certainly see why people would prefer the more varied worldwide selection as well.

#4014. Witcher 3 Remastered Gets Its Next Update On Xbox & PC, Full Patch Notes Revealed

"Two things are certain in a witcher's life: the Path never sleeps, and the work is never done."

Here comes another new patch for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Remastered. The latest update arrived today (November 26) for Xbox Series X|S, PC, PlayStation 5, and Nintendo Switch 2, focusing on "Photo Mode improvements" alongside a hearty batch of fixes.

"Patch 5.02 for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered is now available across PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2! From gameplay and balance and visual adjustments to Photo Mode improvements, to plenty fixes across the Continent and more, this update brings a host of changes to make your adventures on the Path even better."

Most of the fixes revolve around issues with lighting, New Game+, the UI, quests, and Photo Mode. There aren't too many Xbox-specific fixes, but a couple are worth mentioning. These include a fix for achievements not unlocking after transferring PC saves via Cross Progression, as well as intermittent freezing on Xbox Series X|S.

In addition to CD Projekt Red's official fixes, cross-platform mods have just gone live for the Witcher 3 Remastered too! These feature more than 40 mods from community modders, such as boat races, glowing eyes for Geralt, hairstyles and more.

Those are the highlights. We'll leave you with the full patch notes down below.

#4013. Pokémon Winds & Waves Release Date Speculation Rises From Gap In Anime Scheduling

We know that Pokémon Winds and Waves will launch on Switch 2 at some point in 2027, but that's it. The Pokémon Company is still keeping quiet about the upcoming Gen 10 entry, but an announced gap in the long-running anime has some people already narrowing the release window.

Earlier today, it was announced that the Pokémon anime would be taking a whopping nine-month gap between the finale of 'Winter Voyage' in December and a new series starring Liko and Roy, which kicks off in October 2027.

Serebii's Joe Merrick was quick to point out that the anime typically doesn't take breaks like this — usually airing an episode a week, bar some minor gaps. Given that new series of the show typically launch alongside their mainline game, does this mean that there has been a scheduling change at The Pokémon Company, with Winds and Waves being pushed back until later in the year?

For the entirety of my running Serebii there has been a new anime episode each week barring some gaps. For there to be none for 9 months is actually wild. Winds and Waves’ obvious schedule changes really messed with things huh

It certainly seems like a delay behind closed doors is possible — it is strange that TPC would schedule a gap this big in the anime run intentionally. If the upcoming series is set to tie in with Gen 10, then that would put Winds and Waves launching sometime around October 2027.

Hell, any extra time that TPC can be developing the next mainline title gets a big thumbs up from us.

Of course, it could also just be a wild intended pause in the anime, which had no sway on the game at all. TPC always eyes up the big pre-holiday November window for its mainline releases, so who's to say Gen 10 would ever have been any different?

Or things could be really off the wall, and this scheduled anime series is actually nothing to do with Winds and Waves, which TPC could go crazy and release any other time in the year instead!

In short, we're still waiting on something concrete from The Pokémon Company before we know the next release date for sure. But if this anime start date is anything to go by, we imagine we'll be seeing Gen 10 in the same November window that we're used to.

#4012. The Sims 4's much maligned paid mods have made it to consoles, but Kits are coming back to PC

The Sims 4's Marketplace and user-created content have officially arrived on consoles, a little over a month after their debut on PC.

The Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace. This new feature is essentially a hub for paid mods and other user-created content.

As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a new premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.

The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.

For most games, the subject of paid mods has always been fraught, and that's certainly true for The Sims 4. In the announcement blog post, Maxis said that the launch on consoles will work similarly to what PC players have seen, in that Kits will no longer be available to buy directly with real money on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores. While Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs will remain, you’ll need to buy Moola if you want to acquire Kits going forward.

Interestingly, however, EA seems to have changed its mind somewhat on the Kits situation. A recently leaked memo (via SimsCommunity), appears to show that the publisher intends on making Kits available for purchase directly again, without the need for Moola.

Unfortunately, this only appears to affect the PC version, with the reversion reportedly forthcoming on both the EA App as well as Steam. Indeed, according to the same report, the change has already taken place on the former, with the latter following on April 20.

Considering the Marketplace only just launched on consoles, the company may wait to see if the decision to remove Kits from console platform marketplaces will be as poorly received as it has been on PC.

If you’re looking to jump back into The Sims 4 to check out all the new paid content, make sure you’re well-equipped with our list of Sims 4 cheats and debug options, or this one specifically for the Royalty & Legacy expansion cheats.

#4011. Slow down a bit and help a cow find a friend in the lush-looking, hand-drawn, milk deliver-em-up Milki Delivery, which is out now

I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.

The stakes at play in Milki Delivery are very low (as are the steaks, no butchery to be found here, only one very sweet looking cow I couldn't possibly slaughter). You play as Neha, and she's made a promise to her pet cow, the titular Milki, that you'll find her a friend (I think this is a world where there aren't any cows left; yikes!). To do that, all you have to do is deliver her milk! Accept because this is an adventure game, you'll have to help out a few folks along the way.

It's a game very much about the journey, as when riding about this lush and bright countryside, you might find a group of cats that just need a little taste of that sweet creamy juice you've got. Or maybe you have some rope that a farmer needs to wrassle up some sheep. Sometimes you'll have to get a bit more involved with the various people you meet, but predominantly, you'll be delivering milk to folks who need it.

Getting around the place is quite simple too, you plot out your path ahead of time and let the game take you as it's all mouse driven. A relaxed experience to be sure, but the game's art is just so delightful to look at, I'm quite enticed by the idea of just slowing down and enjoying some pretty pictures and making friends along the way. You can make different kinds of milk, too, just be feeding Milki different ingredients. Not how that works in real life, but now I kind of wish it was.

In any case, Milki Delivery is out now, and you can pick it up on Steam.

#4010. Naval warfare, an actual server browser and more on the way to Battlefield 6 this year as BF Studios reveals 2026 roadmap

2026 is looking very exciting for Battlefield 6, even if much of what's coming is based on things we already know, and some we've long been asking for.

It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a plan laid out nonetheless.

The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons currently in the works, and a wealth of new additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.

In a wide-ranging new video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.

The video confirmed that BF6 has at least three other seasons in the works. Season 3, which begins in May, will be followed by Season 4, and Season 5 later in the year. Season 5 is the most mysterious, which is understandable.

We’ve known about some of what’s coming in Season 3, such as the remake of Golmud Railway (now called Railway to Golmud), but the video also revealed that a remake of Battlefield 3’s Grand Bazaar - now Cairo Bazaar - will also arrive later in the same season. Other exciting additions, such as battle royale solos and ranked play for Redsec are also on the agenda for Season 3.

Season 4, set for July, looks to be the biggest so far, with the introduction of naval combat, which will be available across two maps. Tsuru Reef, which is said to be even larger than Golmud, the largest map in BF6. The Pacific-set map won’t be the only one, as later in the season, another remake will arrive, this time of the iconic Wake Island.

The introduction of naval combat will bring with it a new dynamic wave system, aircraft carriers with operational flight decks, and new naval vehicles. Custom lobbies and Spectator Mode are also planned for Season 4.

Season 5 will bring three maps to BF6, rather than two, but all of its content remains under wraps.

Perhaps a sour note is that almost all of the maps referenced and shown in the video are remakes of maps from other Battlefield games, or reimagined at the very least. The Battlefield series is no stranger to remaking its own maps, but Battlefield 6 appears to be leaning on it much more than past entries.

If it’s any consolation, however, the map remakes we’ve played so far in Battlefield 6 have gone through major changes that have contributed to giving them a different flow and feel from their classic versions, or even remakes in other BF games.

Over the course of 2026, you can also expect the return of persistent servers, as well as a server browser to find them all - just like the good ol’ days. This includes the ability to host your own, though it’s unclear quite how this is going to work.

Season 3 is set to revealed in the coming days, so you’ll be hearing back from BF Studios in the near future.

#4009. Diablo 4's next season won't have any new mechanics or a new theme because all the focus is on Lord of Hatred

If you don't intend to buy the Lord of Hatred expansion, the next season in Diablo 4 won't be as exciting as you'd expect.

Diablo 4 is gearing up for its biggest post-launch event yet: the upcoming release of the Lord of Hatred expansion. As was the case with Vessel of Hatred before it, expansion releases alter the seasonal flow in a few ways, and Blizzard has now explained how.

The game’s next season - its 13th - has been officially revealed as Season of Reckoning. The new season will kick off alongside the expansion’s release next week, and will be available to all players, just like all previous seasons.

Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each new season.

You’ll still find the normal Season Rank chase, Smoldering Ashes, and various rewards at each chapter. Season Blessings will also return, but that’s about it for progression outside of the game itself. If it’s any consolation, there are more goals and objectives to tackle this season.

The even better news is that, according to Blizzard, future seasons will follow the classic format, which makes sense. The new season will come with a battle pass, of course, featuring four Reliquaries, as usual. The first Reliquary is free, while the others are paid.

Blizzard has also confirmed the the pre-load for Lord of Hatred is available now on all platforms. Even if you’re not getting the expansion, patch 3.0.0's pre-load includes all expansion content regardless, so you may as well pre-download it to be ready for April 27/28. On launch day, you’ll also need to download a smaller patch, version 3.0.1.

In case you missed it, we published our Lord of Hatred review earlier in the week. Give it a read if you’re curious about the expansion’s impact on the narrative, and how it changes core Diablo 4 gameplay.

#4008. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.8 is refreshing your team comps with a new mechanic, and the game is coming to Steam

Zenless Zone Zero will soon become the first HoYoverse game to make its way to Steam, though we wish we had more details.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a pretty exciting Zenless Zone Zero Special Program that not only delivered all the details on the next big update, it also came with the unexpected announcement that the action RPG is on its way to Steam.

Previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store. In other words, Zenless Zone Zero will soon mark the massive company’s debut on Valve’s platform.

The main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as New Eridan Sunset. This upcoming release is scheduled for May 6, though the Steam version does not yet have a date.The new release sees the release of two new Agents, as well as the brand-new Wind attribute enemy.

The release also acts as the last chapter of Season 2, and it sees Ramiel becoming the main target of different factions in the Outer Ring. The two new arrivals, together with Proxies and Cissia will embark on a quest to learn the new identity of Ramiel.

The first new Agent is Promeia, the executioner of Krampus. She’s an S-Rank Ice Anomaly Agent who can consume Trial by Cold to trigger Abloom on enemies. This is done by converting Corrosive Chill.

By using her EX Special Attack, she can enter the Bound Absolution state, which allows her to automatically Perfect Dodge any attack that targets her. If you have another Anomaly or Support Agent on the team, Promeia can further boost the entire squad’s Abloom damage.

The second addition in 2.8 is Starlight - Billy, also an S-Rank Agent, though wielding Physical Rupture instead. This is the upgraded form of Billy, and he arrives on a combat motorcycle to bring his signature Starlight Knight to the fight. Through it, he can deliver big Physical burst damage.

The higher Billy’s health, the more Sheer damage he deals. In fact, all Physical damage he deals lands as Sheer damage. Further building on his tank-like role, his skills can also restore his own health.

Re-runs in Version 2.8 will be Lucia in the first half, and Orphie & Magus in the second. The other exciting addition coming with this update is the new Wind attribute enemy, and the accompanying Vortex mechanic.

When an enemy is inflicted with the Wind Attribute Anomaly, any other Anomaly attack type that gets applied will trigger Vortex, rather than Disorder. This deals AoE Anomaly damage of the type that matches the corresponding element.

Throughout the version’s runtime, you’ll be able to take part in the Marcel Bootopia-themed event, which gives you control of Eous and lets you explore a Bangboo resort island. The island has been closed due to an outbreak of Hollows, and you must rescue Bangboos and find treasures.

If you do, you’ll earn Booltergeist and its Bangboo core for your troubles. This is an A-Rank Bangboo that can float around and fire lasers in combat. Its damage is further boosted whenever certain teammates are present.

The Ultimate Verdict Trial is another event you can check out that lets you fight alongside newcomer Promeia, or take part in other mini-activities that all reward Polychrome. Finally, you can look forward to a new Hoshimi Miyabi outfit: Dignified Blossom, which will be available in the store.

Before you jump back in next month, it always helps to catch up on the latest Zenless Zone Zero codes to make sure you’re not missing out on any freebies.

#4007. Genshin Impact Luna 7 brings us the first playable Hexenzirkel as things take a turn in Sumeru

Genshin Impact's Luna 7 update will kick off a new Archon Quest chapter, and deliver some interesting new additions to the playable roster.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a new Genshin Impact Special Program, where the developer revealed everything there is to know about the game’s next major update. Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, or as its friends call it, Luna 7, was unveiled as part of the showcase.

This next update has a lot going for it, and it will be in players’ hands everywhere on May 20.

Luna 7 will take us back to Sumeru for its new Archon Quest, where a new crisis that threatens to plunge the nation into chaos is brewing. Nahida is out of the picture, and someone who looks suspiciously like Il Dottore has emerged.

If you complete this chapter at launch, you’ll earn up to 560 Primogems, as well as Nicole's Ascension Materials. Nicole is the first of three playable characters arriving with this update. Something else you’ll unlock if you finish the chapter quickly is a new Weekly Boss that HoYo says has “unpredictable abilities.”

And if you haven’t played in a while, don’t worry, you can refer to the Guiding Notes feature to catch you up on what’s been going on in the world. This is part of a larger effort from the team to make story progression more seamless, and also includes improved quest autosave prompts.

Nicole Reeyn is highest-profile and most interesting, being the first playable member of the Hexenzirkel. The mage is a 5-Star Pyro Catalyst wielder intended as a support member of the team. She can boost the ATK of all party members, even those not currently on the field. She also generates a shield while doing so.

Her Elemental Burst allows her to summon an Arcane Projection that follows the active character, sending out Coordinated Attacks that match their Elemental Type. Outside of combat, Nicole can help you find treasures by calling upon a Seelie to guide you to them. Quite fitting, as you’ll be exploring in the inside of the Witch's Lodge in Nicole’s Meeting Point in Luna 7, so bring her along.

Lohen, the Vice Captain of the Knights of Favonius' Fifth Company, is the second new character. Also a 5-Star addition, he is instead a Cryo Polearm wielder designed for aggressive combat. His main use is dealing massive Cryo DMG, and he can do that by managing two resources unique to him: Joy, and Will to Win.

Through his Elemental Skill, he can enter the Masterstroke state, allowing him to build up (and consume) Joy to unleash enhanced skills. The more his teammates fight, the more Will to Win he biulds, which can later be used to boost his effectiveness further. For an even more powerful display of force, bring along a Hexerei character when he’s on your team.

Prune is the third and final addition. Prune is a 4-Star Anemo Catalyst wielder, and her kit is inspired by her Witch Hunter aspirations. Using a bell and a hammer, she can deal DMG of several elements at once, and trigger Swirl reactions.

Nicole, and Lohen will debut in Luna 7’s first half, while Prune will follow in the second. The first half will also see a Durin rerun, with Mavuika returning in the second half. You can look forward to a new limited-time event as part of Luna 7, with a focus on Klee's Little Hexenzirkel.

You’ll find a series of mini-games you can play alongside Prune, as well as Qiqi, Yaoyao, and Sayu. If you play, you could earn the Super Awesome Magic Key, an exclusive weapon skin. Miliastra Wonderland is doing its thing, too, with a new sports festival for you to take part in.

One new gameplay addition worth calling attention to is that Manekins can now perform actions in Teyvat. The Kamera, which you can use to capture moments with Manekins, is getting upgraded, too, with new editing tools and assets.

Before you pick the game back up, be sure to check out our recently-updated Genshin Impact codes page for some free stuff you may be missing.

#4006. Ex-Nvidia boss Jensen Huang offers to return if that's best for the company and America, Nvidia board essentially say 'nah, we're all good'

New rulers impervious to highly persuasive message of 'come on, please give me my job back, go USA'

Nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a big u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the company and AMERICA.

"On November 12th, our board of directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said during an investors call on November 17th (thanks, Percieving Calls Gamer). "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."

That last bit seems likely to have been said with the intention of quieting down some of the speculation around a Huang return that's been bubbling away since he removed his bum from the black and green throne and that the exec embraced in a statement put out yesterday. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," he wrote. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

"Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. Nvidia is a once-in-a-generation company. If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO."

For now at least, it seems leather jacketed GPUperman will not be triumphantly flying back into his former post amid a wave of corporate and patriotic fervour. Likely as part of continued efforts to reassure moneyfolk that they won't be making negative headlines again soon following Huang's departure, Nvidia's board announced yesterday that they're establishing a "new standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the company’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management". One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government have denied the accusations of espionage.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is currently serving as Nvidia's interim CEO while the company's board searches for a permanent sexy leather jacket man replacement.

#4005. Xbox Console Sales Get A Huge Boost In The UK, While GTA 6 Breaks Records For Physical Games

Series X and S sales received their biggest jump since 2024

We've got some new data coming out about the UK games market in November 2026 today, and unsurprisingly, it's a market that's been absolutely dominated by the launch of GTA 6 last week.

According to the folks at The Game Business, sales of the Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S rose by a whopping 75% during GTA 6's launch week, which represents the biggest jump for Xbox hardware since 2024.

The PS5 was close behind at 46%, and console sales were up 38% overall (after a 29% increase the week before).

In terms of UK console sales, PS5 sales rose 46% during the week GTA 6 came out, while Xbox Series S and X sales jumped 75%. It’s the biggest jump for Xbox since 2024. Overall, UK console sales last week were up 38%, which comes on the back of a 29% increase the week prior.

Meanwhile, the controversial "physical" edition of GTA 6 broke numerous records in Europe, serving as the biggest physical launch in Spain's history according to their charts, and selling over 1m physical copies in France in three days.

It was also the biggest physical launch in the UK since FIFA 20 in September 2019, and is the 17th biggest physical launch since records began there in 1995. This is according to data provided by UK data tracker Nielsen IQ.

"GTA 6 is the biggest physical game launch since 2019, reveals UK data tracker Nielsen IQ. It generated £32 million in revenue in just three days."

Just last week, on the day of GTA 6's release, we mentioned how Xbox hardware spending in the U.S. was up 42% YoY in October, attributed to the likes of Gears of War: E-Day and GTA 6.

It's going to be fascinating to see how the rest of the world stacks up in terms of Xbox sales data from November (which should be revealed over the coming days and weeks), and indeed whether GTA 6's physical edition is also setting records in even more regions. It most likely is - this is a ridiculously popular game after all.

The Witcher 3 Remastered has a new update on PS5, and it's available to download right now, weighing in at a reasonable 1.6GB.

Patch 5.02 is the one many have been waiting for, as it addresses the game's most annoying technical issue on console. I am, of course, referring to the momentary stutters that occurred when autosave was triggered.

This problem was especially noticeable when quest information popped up on the screen, both when you began a quest and finished it. Thankfully, CD Projekt Red's finally taken action.

The patch also improves v-sync and VRR "behaviour" on PS5, which should result in a smoother overall experience. Screen flickering has also been addressed.

On top of those more-than-welcome adjustments, the update is packed with bug fixes — some of which are related to the remaster's new lighting techniques, which could result in some areas looking poorly or incorrectly illuminated.

And in terms of gameplay, we're looking at a bunch of balancing tweaks to a number of Geralt's skills. Some of these perks simply weren't being calculated properly, so you should be more effective in combat right out of the gate with this update installed.

We had our fingers crossed that Team Cherry might reveal the release date for Hollow Knight: Silksong's first DLC in its special presentation today, and what do you know, it did!

Sea of Sorrow will officially launch on Switch and Switch 2 on 11th December. This is a free expansion, so all those with the base game will be able to download and dive right in from this date.

Team Cherry initially teased the DLC late last year, leaving us for 11 months with the vague '2026' release window. It sees Hornet dive into a brand new area of Pharloom, packed with new bosses, tools, enemies and... fishing?

#4002. Mystic Messenger's most loyal players are getting banned in droves for seemingly playing the game too much

With the 10th anniversary of Mystic Messenger nearly upon us, the dating sim has inexplicably begun issuing wide-spread bans for its most active players.

Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years. Despite not receiving new content or any meaningful updates in all that time, the game remains popular with its core fans, many of whom just woke up to some shocking news about their accounts.

The free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts. So far, it looks like players with 1,000 or more have been targeted, but others with far fewer hoards have reported getting the axe, too.

The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.

The message players received is identical, and doesn’t mention the specific reason for the ban. “Your account has been banned because abusive behavior has been detected from your account,” it reads, ending with a support email address the affected user can contact if they believe they’d banned in error.

It didn’t take a while for players to realise that most, if not all of the bans are for players with thousands of Hourglasses in their accounts. The virtual currency can both be acquired in-game just by playing, as well as through direct real-money purchases.

For a nearly ten-year-old game that stopped receiving content three years into its life, it’s easy to see how a dedicated group of players would be able to acquire so many Hourglasses by simply playing regularly for so long.

When contacted by the affected players, Cheritz, the developer and publisher of the game, has instructed them to send receipts of how they acquired Hourglasses (assuming they were purchased) to verify whether or not they’d been fraudulently obtained.

Considering that Mystic Messenger has practically been abandoned by its developer, certain exploits have emerged over the years that allowed players to farm Hourglasses faster than intended, but those instances have always been dealt with then and there.

The blanket and sudden nature of this ban is what’s spooked players, especially those who’ve been logging in for years and never thought accruing in-game currency from playing the game too much would make them the target of a ban.

The running theory is that most of the bans are unintentional, and may be the result of a new automated security system that’s been implemented. It’s entirely possible, especially if its’s AI-based, that the new system simply couldn’t distinguish between those who have earned (or bought) their Hourglasses fairly, and those who used exploits.

The timing of the ban wave is also suspect. With the game’s 10th anniversary coming up in July, it could be that Cheriz is preparing to release a large update for Mystic Messenger, which may include new content. If most of the playerbase is already sitting on massive amounts of in-game currency, they may simply use that to fast-track their way to unlocking the new content, which would greatly affect the developer’s bottom line.

This is a problem that other live service games have run into in the past. Just recently, extraction shooter Arc Raiders added a cap to the amount of Cred players can hold in their accounts very quickly after its launch. That currency is used to buy cosmetic sets in the store, so the logic is easy to follow.

All of that has certainly put a damper on the enthusiasm of the game’s most active players, many of whom were excited to get together in person for the coming 10th anniversary, participate in community nights and so on to celebrate.

It’s also disheartening to see a fanbase so loyal; playing a game as regularly for so long without new content, to be treated so poorly. Even without knowing what the game is, it’s impressive that so many people have kept the flag of their favourite game flying for so long.

To find out how this dating system works, here’s a Mystic Messenger primer that explains it all. Once you’ve wrapped your head around it, you’ll no doubt want to pick the correct answers for every guest, and this guide will help you nail every one.

#4001. Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt MindsEye devs Build a Rocket Boy are splurging on legal action against "a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews"

Administrators say "a substantial litigation fund is anticipated to arise"

Freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the company's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors. The documents also touch on founder Leslie Benzies and CEO Mark Gerhard's claims that MindsEye is the victim of an organised sabotage campaign. The company's leaders have apparently taken out even more loans in order to fund legal action against the suspected perpetrators, with the promise of a healthy payout. I'm not holding my breath.

BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals. Asset manager Diameter Capital Partners are the second largest external creditor, having loaned BARB around £4.25 million. A further $19 million is owed to "group undertakings" – "group undertakings" meaning debts to parent companies, subsidiaries or fellow subsidiaries. Studio founder Benzies, meanwhile, is owed £1,158,167.05. Given that Benzies has been repeatedly accused of torpedoing MindsEye's fortunes by way of disruptive micro-management, I'm not sure many BARB staff would agree that he really deserves his million quid back at this stage, but that's what it says on paper. Smaller IOUs include £10,434.11 for Amazon Web Services, £634.36 for Unity, and a mighty £19.90 for OpenAI.

Build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say. Announced in 2023, their flagship project MindsEye is a filmic GTA-ish action shooter initially billed as a full-fat demo for Everywhere, a game creation platform comparable to Roblox. MindsEye struggled to compel us before launch and did not find its people on release, with poor sales leading to layoffs even as BARB leadership insisted they could revive the game's fortunes.

The same leadership were subsequently accused by their own staff of "disastrously" mishandling the redundancies and enforcing "unbearable" crunch. Unionised BARB employees have now taken management to court for installing alleged surveillance software on their work PCs. The game's publishers Io Interactive noped out of the picture in March this year. Meanwhile, Benzies and Gerhard have thrown around accusations of a sinister espionage and sabotage campaign, carried out by unspecified perpetrators. They made a sort of revenge fantasy DLC pack about it, which our own Mark Warren characterised as we-already-have-Hitman-at-home. The bankruptcy documents shed more light on these twists and turns. According to the administrators, BARB were "funded mainly by equity investment from institutional, strategic and venture capital investors over several funding rounds, including a $110m Series D round in 2023." This followed a £32 million investment in 2020, as reported by GI. The company grew significantly during MindsEye's creation to around 500 UK and overseas employees. According to a group income statement, the company posted sequential operating losses of £47.5 million for the period ending September 30th, 2025, and £63.1 million for the year ending December 2024. The administrator proposals document also devotes some time to the aforesaid allegations of sabotage. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary," it reads. "The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions." A later section vaguely alludes to the sum BARB leadership hope to recover. "Prior to the Joint Administrators' appointment, the Company had undertaken detailed investigations and had commenced litigation against several third parties, with the assistance of the Company's former legal advisers, Brandsmiths, in connection with matters described earlier in the Proposals," the doc reads. "The Joint Administrators consider the litigation potentially to be the largest asset of the Administration." The document goes on that BARB management have "sought financial support from third party investors to fund the anticipated legal costs and expenses associated with the litigation", with some of these funding agreements already executed. "Further executed agreements and associated funding contributions are expected to be received, shortly, and a substantial litigation fund is anticipated to arise," it continues. The Joint Administrators are "currently engaging in the on-going litigation, progressing the funding arrangements entered into by the Company, and have assessed the merits of pursuing the litigation". They will liaise with relevant parties to "determine the most appropriate strategy for preserving and, where appropriate, realising value from this potential asset for the benefit of creditors and other stakeholders." The doc doesn't name who, exactly, is being taken to court. As far as I'm aware, it isn't us. Anyway, it's good to know that the company who owe over £60 million are taking on more debt in order to pursue a histrionic grievance for which they have yet to supply any real evidence whatsoever.

#4000. Forza Horizon 6 explodes on Steam even before it's officially out

Forza Horizon 6 looks to have easily delivered the most successful launch for any game in the series on PC, with record-breaking player numbers.

Steam is abuzz this week with a couple of long-anticipated launches, but in Forza Horizon 6’s case, at least, the game isn’t even out for what will be most of its players. The anticipated sequel in the open-world driving game series doesn’t officially launch until May 19, but owners of its most expensive version - the Premium Edition - can play it right now.

That version of the game includes more than just a few days of early access, of course, but you’d think the $120 price tag would’ve only been palatable to a small group of players. Not the case with this game.

Forza Horizon 6, which has spent 16 weeks in Steam’s global top sellers list, currently occupies the number two spot, having jumped up three spots this week in anticipation of the launch. The game has also naturally been popular with players, so popular in fact that it has already overtaken the player counts of all other Horizon games on the platform.

At the time of writing, the game has peaked at 128,157 concurrent players on Steam alone (via SteamDB). The figure has already climbed several times during the writing of this story, so you can only imagine how much higher it’s going to get deeper into the weekend.

All of that, of course, days before the official launch on Tuesday, when, theoretically, the majority of the game’s audience will be able to start playing. In just a few short hours, Horizon 6 has already gone well above Forza Horizon 5’s peak concurrent of 81,096, as well as Forza Horizon 4’s peak 75,689 players.

Steam is the only platform that publishes player numbers, of course, but it’s easy to see how similar the enthusiasm is going to be on Xbox. Though the game is not yet part of the Game Pass line-up, those who don’t want to wait could buy the Premium Edition Upgrade to get the included content, and play it right now.

Game Pass, and Xbox / Windows Store numbers don’t factor into Steam’s, which is another thing to consider when viewing the numbers holistically. Indeed, given how successful Forza Horizon 5 has been on PlayStation 5, Horizon 6’s upcoming release on Sony's console is bound to be even bigger.

Forza Horizon 5 has been off to a similarly flying start in the first few days of its own advanced access launch, so it’s obviously not surprising to see Horizon 6 do better there. In case you missed it, check out our review of Forza Horizon 6. In short, we really liked it, even if we expected more.

#3999. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.3 will take us deeper into the World in Canvas and make Mortenax Blade playable

Honkai: Star Rail's next big outing will see the continuation of the Planarcadia story, and it's going to be with us soon.

HoYoverse has today delivered full details on the next major update for Honkai: Star Rail. Version 4.3, dubbed The Lethe Below the Living, will be available for all players on June 1. The upcoming update adds a new chapter to the Planarcadia arc, and introduce a new playable character.

The new narrative chapter will also unveil more about Mortenax Blade, the Trailblazer themselves, and the husk of the Aeon.

Mortenax Blade is the hero of this chapter, and he’s going to step into the World in Canvas. The goal is to - by borrowing the power of Voracity - excise Shuhu from his body and end the curse.

The Trailblazer goes on a trip of their own in Version 4.3, this time to Inkford Hermitage, right on the edge between the World in Canvas and the real world. They’re going to undertake this journey to warn Graphia of the Asat Pramad threat.

In case you hadn’t already guessed, Mortenax Blade is this version’s new playable character. The 5-Star Fire-Type swordsman is on the Path of Nihility. Blade’s Ultimate allows him to enter an enhanced state by deploying a special Bounded Field.

While the field is active, all enemies receive more DMG. Entering this state is also how Blade unlocks his skill, which uses a Sword Formation to deal more damage. This is then used to essentially unlock a second, more powerful Ultimate for him.

The benefits of Mortenax Blade’s kit extend to his teammates, too. Any ally who attacks an enemy with him on the team, they inflict a debuff on them. This also builds up a special Charge that Blade can later use with his Skill.

Version 4.3’s launch arrives alongside the Gift of Tempered Blade event. Through it, you can claim a new Trailblazer Outfit piece for free, but only after getting Mortenax Blade from Warping. The first phase’s rerun will be Yao Guang, and the second phase will bring back both Cyrene and Phainon.

You can also expect the Wispae Amusement Park to arrive within the World in Canvas, which you’ll get to design. You can plan where the rides will go, pick the different themes, set visitor routes and more.

Starward Mode is another new addition, which can be found in Memory of Chaos, Pure Fiction, and Apocalyptic Shadow. Starward will see you take on three different stages, which you’ll need three teams for. Clearing each challenge with full stars will reward you 100 Stellar Jades extra per chase.

There’s more coming down the line, too. A new Fate/Stay Night [Unlimited Blade Works] collaboration will arrive in a content up this summer. The event will give players a chance to earn Gilgamesh or Archer for free by logging in.

#3998. Analyst Suggests Console Prices Won't Drop Until At Least 2028

"If data centre demand grows, then it could quickly eat into the extra supply"

We've grumbled about the rising cost of Xbox consoles in recent months, as I'm sure you have too. But if you were hoping 2027 would be the year things finally get cheaper, well, according to S&P boffins, it doesn't look likely.

Recently, the gang over at GamesIndustry.biz spoke with S&P analyst Neil Barbour about the AI industry's all-consuming demand for DRAM, rising console costs, and when launching new consoles at affordable prices points might finally become a reality again.

According to S&P Global Market Intelligence Kagan, DRAM capacity is projected to reach "184,000mm-equivalent wafers by the end of this year, 434,000 by the end of 2027, before rising exponentially to 819,000 in 2028".

"[2028 is] the earliest point at which launching new consoles at accessible price points looks prudent,"

In layman's terms, these digits suggest supply might finally begin catching up with demand in 2028, potentially bringing down the cost of PCs and consoles.

DRAM is essentially a console or PC's super-fast short-term memory. Whenever you boot a game, its data is loaded into DRAM so it can be accessed and processed quickly. The more DRAM you have, the bigger and more ambitious games you can play.

The image above gives us a breakdown of the additional DRAM supply expected from each manufacturer, pointing to 2028 as the earliest point at which prices could start to get smaller.

However, that's relying on a consistent demand from data centres. If it continues to grow, all that additional DRAM could be gobbled up by the AI industry. Likewise, if demand is less popular than predicted, supplies could return quicker.

"If data centre demand grows, then it could quickly eat into the extra supply...The memory [fabrication facilities] are not expanding with an eye specifically toward the consumer market. They're racking up record revenue and margins on the data centre build-out, so these supply expansions are primarily meant to feed that demand."

Microsoft's next-gen Xbox Helix console is rumoured to be launching in 2028 with a suspected price tag of over $1,000. Barbour weighed in on Microsoft's Xbox Series supply shortages.

"If Microsoft is suffering from supply shortages with the current Series consoles, as it has said a few times over the past year, then they will almost have to wait for the upstream component supply to shore up before they make a big push with a new console."

#3997. Monopoly Go x The Simpsons crossover is almost here

After a long wait and exhaustive leaks, the highly-anticipated Simpsons event will finally arrive in Monopoly Go very soon, alongside new content.

Monopoly Go players have been looking forward to a major crossover event for what felt like months, and though most of the details ended up leaking, nothing actually beats official information.

The world of The Simpsons has officially arrived in Monopoly Go, and there's a whole lot for players to dive into. The show's creative team even produced a new animated short, featuring Mr. Monopoly, and Mr. Burns.

Available June 3 through July 29, the new event allows Monopoly Go players to jump in the world of The Simpsons. You'll be able to build, and explore all around multiple iconic locations from the show.

Along the way, you'll run into Simpsons characters like Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, and of course, Mr. Burns. Developer Scopely teamed up with the show's creative team to create many references, and Easter Eggs for you to discover. You'll find some of those on chance cards, but most of the world has been changed to be part of The Simpsons, including getting to bribe Chief Wiggum to escape jail.

The developer promises a deeply connected world with Simpsons narratives and characters that alter seasonal maps, and offer unique sticker sets and animated sequences to dive in. Incidentally, this is The Simpsons' first appearance in a mobile-exclusive game in 13 years.

Here's a breakdown of everything you can expect, straight from Scopely:

Episodes: Narrative-driven encounters that create stories inspired by The Simpsons. Episodes play out across seasonal boards, sticker sets, and minigames, all capped off with an animated short.

Sticker sets: Every Episode comes with its own limited-time sticker set, taking cues from the latest Simpsons story. Collectible artwork, character journeys and other rewards are yours to claim for the duration of each Episode.

The Simpsons Run: Every two weeks, a new Springfield character will take over the Free Parking tile, kicking off character-driven runs.

Simpsons-themed Shutdowns and Heists: Monopoly Go's shutdowns and heists get a Simpsons makeover, with Springfield-inspired chaos and disasters.

Bribe Wiggum: This changes Go to Jail to allow players to bribe Chief Wiggum, giving you a chance to earn a bigger reward, but not without introducing an element of unpredictability.

Simpsons chance cards: The chance card collection grows with over 50 Simpsons-themed cards full of memes, references and one-liners from the show.

#3996. PC remains GTA 6's last hope for 60fps smoothness as Rockstar confirm such an option isn't coming to even the swankiest consoles

Poor little game boxes just can't handle it

As you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware. Despite reports claiming one may not be far away, there's still no official word on a PC port, hence why we've not got a review that delves deep into analysis of just how central to the experience the smell reaction system is.

The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.

Speaking to Kotaku, GTA 6's devs made clear optional 60 or 40fps performance modes aren't on the way, even for the more powerful Pro variant of the PS5.

"Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)," Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers put it. "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates."

So, there you go. The consoles just ain't got that dog in 'em. One would think, then, that being able to run GTA 6 in all its glory at higher frame rates will likely be a selling point for that PC port that's assumed to be on the way. Whether the average PC owner's graphics card and other bits will have the horses to deliver a smooth 60 is another question, and an especially pertinent one given the ongoing RAM crisis has made upgrading certain aspects of your setup ludicrously expensive.

If it requires a 5090 at a minimum, I guess those of us with less than absolute cutting edge cards will just have to keep playing Sleeping Dogs until the AI bubble bursts.

#3995. GTA 6 Gives PS5 a Very Rare Win Over Switch 2 in Japan

At this point, it’s well known that Switch 2 is by far the market leader in Japan.

While the PS5 still commands some marketshare, it gets dominated by the Nintendo machine on a weekly basis.

GTA 6’s launch is significant, then, because for the first time in a while it’s pushed Sony’s console in front of the Switch 2 – albeit only by a few thousand units.

According to Famitsu’s latest report, the PS5 sold 41,472 units through the week ending 22nd November, while the Switch 2 managed 36,817 units.

This is an incredibly rare scenario, and likely won’t be repeated again (if ever). But it shows that with the right software, Sony can put up a fight domestically against Nintendo.

The company’s been taking the region a lot more seriously under Japanese CEO Hideaki Nishino, launching more affordable region locked units to try and stimulate interest.

This week saw the release of the new Midnight Black model, which certainly helped contribute to the sales.

But PS5’s success was primarily motivated by GTA 6, which sold a very respectable 200,759 units at retail for the week.

That’s slightly less than GTA 5’s 304,752 units opening in 2013, although remember digital buying habits have changed dramatically in the last 13 years, and GTA 6’s physical release was not particularly compelling as it doesn’t include a disc.

A good week for Sony in its home region, then – one that’s unlikely to be replicated, but should be taken as a sign it can compete with the right lineup and pricing model.

The Cherry Time! showcase promised "a bunch of exciting announcements," and these were not Hollow Knight-related (until the last one, of course), but instead focused on a handful of titles coming out under the studio's publishing arm.

We've got the trailer and info for each of the three games included below, but honestly, what a wholesome way for Team Cherry to use its indie power! We came for Silksong DLC news (and we got it), but we left with another three games to add to our wishlists.

#3993. Chronicles: Medieval devs Raw Power are bankrupt, but their sandbox RPG lives on at a new studio co-founded by Satisfactory devs Coffee Stain

It "ticks many of the boxes", despite the funding problems

Goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games. The game will now be made by a new developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.

In development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time. It sees you positioning archers behind spears and finessing your cavalry flanking actions, all the while occupying a fleshy human body that can be hacked and stabbed. It's set during the Hundred Years' War between England and France over the 14th and 15th centuries, and gives you a volatile sandbox world of warring factions and patrols.

The original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions. It's not entirely clear who has made the leap to Coffee Stain's newly founded studio.

Raw Power declared bankruptcy on 30th October, subsequently calling on players to help them find funding. During the bankruptcy proceedings, Coffee Stain successfully bid 36.75 million Danish Krone for Chronicles: Medieval, which comes to around four million pounds or 5.4 million dollars. According to CEO Anton Westbergh the project "ticks many of the boxes that we believe to be fundamental for a great game, and we think it has a good chance of becoming a strong long-term IP for the group." The game yet sits at 26th on SteamDB's most wishlisted, despite Raw Power's funding troubles.

Gaming doesn't want for simulations of shrieking feudal folk, but Medieval has a certain swagger, even when you remove Tom Hardy from the picture (and you should - he only ever voiced that one trailer). Here's hoping the new team can find their feet under Coffee Stain, and that whoever hasn't made the transition finds good work elsewhere.

#3992. Xbox CSO Responds To Criticism Around Game Branding, Promises To Fix In 2027

"We are fixing this. Will roll out in 2027."

Every now and again, we hear grumbles from some parts of the Xbox community that they're frustrated when games are announced and Xbox doesn't make a big deal about how those titles are specifically first-party creations.

In other words, some fans want Xbox to shout from the rooftops about its own games for its own platform, and not to make them immediately look like third-party titles. There's been some discussion about this on social media this week with Xbox megafan Klobrille and Windows Central editor Jez Corden, highlighting situations like StarCraft, Diablo V and new Fallout games where it felt like they were announced without any real references to Xbox.

And, when Corden stated that "Xbox is really weak at linking its games to its brand", it prompted Xbox CSO Matthew Ball to get involved in the discussion and promise that the situation is being fixed in 2027.

Who knows what "fixed" means in this regard, but it sounds like the team at Xbox is going to be more proactive at promoting the brand when an Xbox Game Studios, Activision Blizzard or Bethesda title is announced / shown off.

That doesn't necessarily mean anything in terms of exclusives and multi-platform titles (we assume we'll still get some of the latter), but hopefully it'll be much clearer to the average consumer when a game is an in-house Xbox game.

Let's see what happens in the New Year, eh? We've got Fable just around the corner in a couple of months' time, and then the likes of Clockwork: Revolution and Spyro: A Realm Reborn (which is only published by Xbox, but nevertheless still counts!) along with whatever else Xbox might have in store for us in 2027.

#3989. Hitman, 007 First Light PS5 Crossover Makes Lenny Kravitz Your New Ally

It's a bit surprising this crossover hasn't already happened, to be honest, given IO Interactive is the studio behind both of the games, but it's now been confirmed a Hitman and 007 First Light collaboration is happening.

The content is live from today until 24th December 2026, and it takes the form of a new Elusive Target in Hitman. Lenny Kravitz, who is playing Bawma from 007 First Light, is the next celebrity to feature in Hitman, but this time, he's on Agent 47's side.

Bawma has been betrayed by three of his associates, and he's called in the bald assassin to take them down.

Up for elimination are Horace Stockton, Oswald Spoon, and Zui.

The new set of Elusive Targets and the mission hosting them brings with it the likeness and voice of Lenny Kravitz, who you'll hear from throughout the level via Agent 47's earpiece.

"Bawma is such a fun and interesting character to portray, so I was excited to step back into a new world with him for 007 First Light," said Kravitz. "Seeing Bawma team up with Agent 47 is something I think fans of both games are going to love."

The mission will be available until 24th December, but if you own a copy of the game, then you'll retain permanent access to the Arcade version of it. It can also be accessed free of charge for those who don't have Hitman 3, as it's being added to the demo of the game.

Review Hitman 3 (PS5) - The Ultimate Stealth Sandbox

Alongside the mission, a roadmap detailing the Season of Bawma teases the following content additions: a new Escalation, new Arcade and Special Assignment contracts, a new challenge, a batch of Featured Contracts, a new Twitch Drop and an IOI Account reward.

Will you team up with Lenny Kravitz to take down his associates? Let us know in the comments below.

"We're still in the early stages of what we want to achieve"

In a first substantial update since acquiring SteamDB from its founders back in September, the owners of Nexus Mods have outlined some new additions coming to , the two sides in the deal have announced some additions coming to the community-run backend database. Affiliate links aimed at providing options to help folks find the cheapest price for a game and a new tab dedicated to the mods Nexus host for a game are incoming, as work on behind-the-scenes improvements continues.

"We're now a couple of months in since [the takeover] announcement, so I thought it was about time we shared a quick update on what we've been working on behind the scenes, along with a few changes you'll start to see rolling out over the coming weeks," Victor Folmann, CEO of Nexus Mods owners Chosen wrote in a blog post on SteamDB.

There are two main new features he pointed to that you'll notice popping up on SteamDB soon. The first is one that anyone could have seen coming, a new tab on each moddable game's page that shows off some mods hosted for it on Nexus Mods and a host of modding-related data. "The new tab will help you discover mods for games you're browsing on SteamDB, making it easier to see whether a game has an active modding community and explore what it has to offer," Fomann wrote. "For now, we'll only be showing mods from Nexus Mods, as we already have access to that wealth of modding data, making it a straightforward starting point for this new feature.

"We appreciate that some of you might be wondering why we're not including Steam Workshop, too. It's certainly something we'd be open to exploring as we develop the feature further, along with other modding sources. With that in mind, if you run a modding website and would be interested in having your community's mods included, we'd love to hear from you."

That seems perfectly fine, but the other incoming feature's a bit more controversial given SteamDB's historically not been all about the money. "One thing we've seen people ask for is an easier way to find the cheapest place to buy a game, and we're now working on making that possible," Folmann wrote. "We'll be introducing affiliate links to authorised game retailers, giving you more options when looking for the best available price on a game.

"We recognise that introducing affiliate links may raise some concerns, so we want to be clear about how they'll work. First and foremost, as I mentioned, we'll only feature authorised retailers; we will not be including grey-market resellers. We've also made a deliberate decision about how prices are displayed: retailers will be ordered by the cheapest available price in your currency, not by whichever retailer offers us the highest affiliate commission. If a retailer doesn't offer pricing in your currency, we'll still show deals in other currencies provided they are available in your region."

Folmann was clear in the initial announcement of the takeover that Nexus Mods' bosses would be actively looking into ways SteamDB could make more money to sustain itself, so the addition of these links isn't out of the blue either. Whether SteamDB regulars agree that they're a "lighter-touch" way of earning the site some cash without detracting from the traditional experience of using it is another matter. I'll need to see how I feel once I've actually navigated a few pages with the links in as part of looking up stuff about games, but my first instinct is that as long as the pages don't end up revolving around the links and it's still easy to get to the info you want without interacting with them, I probably won't be too put out.

Beyond those tweaks, Folmann mentioned "improvements to how updates are tested before they go live" and how quickly the team can react to issues have been among the less obvious work going on behind the scenes. "We're still in the early stages of what we want to achieve, and there's plenty more work we need to do and would like to work on," he wrote in closing.

Folmann and co only took over Nexus Mods in June last year, making them still relatively new custodians of both it and SteamDB.

#3987. GTA 6 developers at Rockstar are worried about being laid off after shipping "the biggest game of all time"

Rockstar has successfully shipped Grand Theft Auto 6, after years of work and more than a billion dollars spent. GTA 6 is already one of the highest-rated games ever - Eurogamer awarded it five stars in our GTA 6 review - and it's expected to be among the most successful, best-selling games ever.

But that may not be enough to prevent layoffs at Rockstar, some people working within the studio fear. Nestor Uriarte, an animation programmer at Rockstar North, wrote about their concern for their job and those of their colleagues in an article on The Guardian.

"After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it's hard not to worry about what the future holds," Uriarte wrote. "It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised."

Uriarte's piece comes as Rockstar staff's efforts to establish a union reach a critical point. A tribunal between the studio and fired IWBG union members just concluded, though the verdict may not arrive for many weeks or months.

Rockstar's UK studios are currently voting on recognising an official Rockstar workers union. Uriarte is in support of it and has urged colleagues to vote in favour of it. Results of that vote are expected today.

"Winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar, but its significance would reach far beyond that," Uriarte pointed out.

"As one of the biggest and most influential game studios in the world, what happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry - one in which workers' voices are taken into account more."

Across its 12 offices around the world, Rockstar's headcount grew to 4,711 during GTA 6's development - double its size when it released Red Dead Redemption 2.

As popular and profitable as Rockstar's games are, the company has initiated layoffs in the past after shipping a major project. While there's no way of knowing whether the same is going to happen for GTA 6, the justifiable concerns - given the current state of the industry - are there. According to the ASGC Games Industry Layoffs Tracker, more than 12,000 developers have lost their jobs this year so far, up from more than 9,000 people last year.

#3986. "It’s hard not to worry": Even as GTA 6 launches on console amid glowing reviews, Rockstar devs are already concerned about getting laid off

Even though they've "had no indication that layoffs are coming" from bosses

GTA 6 launches on console today. It's widely expected to sell more copies than main character Lucia Caminos has skin pores, more copies than there are words even in Eurogamer's five-star review, which I believe Chris Tapsell has written specifically to exhaust and destroy such neurones as I have remaining. And yet, staff at Rockstar Games are apparently worrying about being laid off, as development winds down and investors start to bicker about Line Going Up Even More.

In an article supporting this month's union vote at Rockstar North, one of the game's animation programmers argues that "workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised."

The animation programmer in question is Nestor Uriarte, writing in The Guardian's Comment Is Free section. Following some personal reflections on his time at the studio, he calls on other Rockstar devs to get behind the union, describing it as both "a huge step forward" for a company that has previously faced allegations of "crunch culture", and a win for UK game developers at large. "What happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry – one in which workers’ voices are taken into account more," Uriarte writes.

The vote at Rockstar North will run till 26th November, and could give rise to a union spanning over 1600 developers, according to umbrella organisation the Independent Workers of Great Britain. If that comes to pass, it would make the Rockstar union the largest recognised videogame developer union in the UK.

It comes as the company and a group of fired workers await the result of an employment tribunal battle over alleged "union-busting". Rockstar has accused the workers in question of "gross misconduct" and a breach of confidentiality by means of a union Discord server. Amongst other things, the legal brawl has revealed that Rockstar had a mole on that server for two and a half years, prior to the firings.

As for the prospect of further job losses, after GTA 6 goes on sale, Uriarte cites a wave of mass layoffs across the industry that has affected the creators of even commercially successful games like Battlefield 6 and Netflix's FIFA World Cup.

"After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it’s hard not to worry about what the future holds," he writes. "Studios across the industry have been slashing huge portions of their workforces, with an estimated 24,000 roles axed globally over the last two years. It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised."

The obvious context here is that GTA 6 has been a massively expensive production, with a development team headcount in the thousands. While one could accuse Uriarte of fear-mongering, I do find it hard to believe that executives at parent company Take-Two aren't weighing up some timely "down-sizing" right now. In general, videogame companies have a long tradition of axing the books once a game has been shipped, despite arguments that keeping experienced teams intact often pays off. In Rockstar's case, however, it's also worth bearing in mind that the GTA 6 rolling out this week is only part of the package. There's also the hazy prospect of the next incarnation of GTA Online, which – going by GTA 5 sales – will be a money spinner for many years, and will require a sizeable staff to maintain. Oh, and of course there's the PC version.

Echoing many peers, Uriarte also argues in his piece that it's important to unionise now in order to negotiate proper protection against generative AI cost-cutting initiatives. "The rapid emergence of AI is transforming how studios work and raising fundamental questions about the future of our industry," he continues. "Across the sector, the skills that workers spend years developing risk being devalued as their creative work is replaced by AI.

"Rockstar has said it is committed to preserving jobs and it has been clear that our games will continue to be made by people," Urirarte concedes. "But with recognition we’d have a seat at the table to manage this industry-wide transition together."
